round_2_revision_note: Amends round-1 per architecture-critic's BLOCKED verdict (tasks/agent-outputs/architecture-critic/FEAT-5.json). Both required fixes are folded into the design below, not left as implementation-time surprises: (1) Critical — added a new `sortColumn` table-descriptor property so the shared GET / list query's ORDER BY is no longer hardcoded to `name`, since migration 0013 drops resource_cost.name; verified directly against the live backend/src/masterDataRouter.js line `order by (deleted_at is not null), name asc` and backend/src/masterDataTables.js's MASTER_DATA_TABLES shape (both Read directly, not taken on a prior stage's word). (2) Important — the lookups LEFT JOIN condition now explicitly includes `and j.deleted_at is null` so a soft-deleted resource correctly yields a null employeeName/employeeDesignation instead of stale data, matching what round 1's prose already claimed but the join clause didn't actually implement.
summary: Solution Design Document for Resource Cost's real schema (employeeId FK to resources.employee_id, live-lookup employeeName/employeeDesignation, independently-optional offshoreCost/onsiteCost). Constrained by tech-lead's FEAT-5 direction (generalized validateExists + lookup descriptor kinds, defense-in-depth DB FK + app-layer check, FK index, thin MCP layer, Employee-prefixed frontend labels) and database.md/api.md/frontend.md. No application code written at this stage per solution-architect.md's scope (SDD only) — schema/component structuring belongs to stage 3.3 (System Engineer), implementation to stage 3.5/4 (Engineer/Developer), and the migration must still be authored + applied live at those later stages, not here.
scope_note: Stage 3 produces the design document that stages 3.1 (Architecture Critic), 3.3 (System Engineer) and 3.5 (Engineer/MVP) build from. No file was created or edited by this stage; all paths below are targets for later stages.

validateExists.attached_to: a single field entry in MASTER_DATA_TABLES[*].fields (backend only) — e.g. the resource_cost table's employeeId field gets validateExists: { table: 'resources', column: 'employee_id' }
validateExists.generality: keyed purely by table/column name, never hardcoded to resource_cost/resources, so resource_deployment's future employeeId field (flagged by tech-lead as a likely sibling need) can reuse it by adding the same descriptor to its own field entry — zero new code required.
validateExists.enforcement_point: masterDataSchema.js gains a new async function, e.g. validateReferences(table, body, { partial }), called from masterDataRouter.js's POST and PATCH handlers immediately after the existing synchronous validateBody(). For each field with validateExists that is present in the request (required-on-create, present-on-update per the same partial-update semantics validateBody already uses), it runs `select 1 from ${ref.table} where ${ref.column} = $1 and deleted_at is null` and throws validationError({ [field.key]: '<key> must reference an existing, non-deleted <ref.table> row.' }) — a 422 per api.md, not a 404 (this is a bad request body, not a missing resource-by-id lookup) and not a generic '<resource>_not_found' (that code is reserved for notFound(), used for id-in-URL lookups).
validateExists.why_not_reuse_notFound: notFound() is shaped around 'the resource in the URL path doesn't exist'; this is a body-field reference check, so a dedicated validation_error under details[field.key] keeps api.md's error-shape distinction between 404 (URL resource missing) and 422 (request body invalid) intact.
validateExists.must_run_before_insert: app-layer check runs before the INSERT/UPDATE statement executes, so a bad employeeId never reaches Postgres and never risks surfacing as a raw FK-violation 500 — this satisfies tech-lead's 'app-layer check must run first' ordering requirement.
validateExists.soft_delete_semantics: deleted_at is null is mandatory in the existence check — a soft-deleted resource must not be a valid FK target, matching how PATCH/DELETE already refuse to act on soft-deleted rows elsewhere in masterDataRouter.js.
validateExists.not_applied_to_modules_practiceId: modules.practiceId keeps its current unvalidated behavviour untouched — validateExists is opt-in per field descriptor, so this is additive-only and does not change any of the other 8 tables.

lookup.attached_to: the table descriptor itself (a new top-level property on the resource_cost entry in MASTER_DATA_TABLES), not a field entry — because employeeName/employeeDesignation are never persisted, never validated, and never part of the INSERT/UPDATE column list. e.g. resource_cost's descriptor gains: lookups: { table: 'resources', on: 'employee_id', select: { employeeName: 'name', employeeDesignation: 'designation' } }
lookup.generality: same table/column-keyed shape as validateExists so it composes with it (both point at 'resources'/'employee_id') and so resource_deployment can add the identical lookups block later without new router code.
lookup.read_path_change: masterDataRouter.js's GET list and GET one handlers change their SQL only when table.lookups is present: instead of `select * from ${tableName}`, they build `select t.*, ${aliasedSelectColumns} from ${tableName} t left join ${lookups.table} j on j.${lookups.on} = t.${lookups.on} and j.deleted_at is null where ...` (LEFT JOIN, not INNER — a resource_cost row whose employeeId matches no resource, e.g. after the referenced resource is later soft-deleted or hard-removed by some future process, must still be listed rather than silently vanishing; employeeName/employeeDesignation simply come back null in that edge case, matching the existing 'row.column may be null' shape everywhere else in this file). ROUND-2 FIX (architecture-critic Important finding): the join predicate now explicitly includes `and j.deleted_at is null` alongside the equality condition — round 1's prose claimed a soft-deleted resource yields null lookup fields, but the join clause as originally specified had no deleted_at predicate and would have still matched (and returned stale name/designation from) a soft-deleted resources row, since a soft delete only sets deleted_at and never removes the row. Query builds the join condition off `lookups.on` generically (not hardcoded to employee_id), and the aliasedSelectColumns come from `lookups.select`'s values (e.g. `j.name as employee_name, j.designation as employee_designation`), so the SQL is generated from the descriptor, not written bespoke per table.
lookup.other_tables_unaffected: the 8 tables with no `lookups` property keep the exact current `select * from ${tableName}` query untouched — this is the conditional branch tech-lead required to keep the change additive rather than a regression risk to the shared factory.
lookup.toResponse_change: masterDataSchema.js's toResponse(table, row) gains: after the existing field-by-field loop, `if (table.lookups) for (const [responseKey, sourceCol] of Object.entries(table.lookups.select)) response[responseKey] = row[snake_case_alias_of(sourceCol)]` — reading off the joined/aliased columns the new SQL selected (e.g. row.employee_name -> response.employeeName), not off `table.fields`, since these two keys deliberately never appear in `fields[]`.
lookup.not_writable: because employeeName/employeeDesignation are never added to resource_cost's `fields[]` array, validateBody/the INSERT column list/the UPDATE SET clause never reference them — a client POST/PATCH body containing employeeName is silently ignored (same behavior as sending any other unknown key today), which is correct: these are read-only projections, not editable inputs, per the requirement.

sortColumn.round_2_addition: New table-descriptor property, added in direct response to architecture-critic's Critical finding. Shape: a single string, the snake_case column name the shared GET / list handler should ORDER BY. Optional; when absent, the router falls back to `'name'`, so all 8 existing tables (practices, delivery_centers, competencies, modules, resources, departments, teams, resource_deployment) need zero changes to keep their current, unmodified sort behavior.
sortColumn.enforcement_point: masterDataRouter.js's GET / handler changes its hardcoded `order by (deleted_at is not null), name asc` to `order by (deleted_at is not null), ${table.sortColumn ?? 'name'} asc`. `table.sortColumn` comes only from the fixed MASTER_DATA_TABLES allow-list (never request input), so interpolating it is exactly as safe as the existing `tableName`/`column` interpolation this file already documents in its header comment — no new injection surface.
sortColumn.resource_cost_value: resource_cost's descriptor sets `sortColumn: 'employee_id'`. Rationale: employee_id is required (NOT NULL) on every resource_cost row post-migration, always present (unlike offshoreCost/onsiteCost, which are independently optional and would sort inconsistently with nulls), and gives a meaningful, stable ordering (cost rows grouped by employee) rather than an incidental one like created_at/insertion order. It survives the migration that drops `name`, resolving the Critical finding: after 0013 lands, `select * from resource_cost order by (deleted_at is not null), employee_id asc ...` is valid SQL against the post-migration schema.
sortColumn.why_not_created_at: created_at was the architecture-critic's alternate suggestion, but employee_id is preferred here because it's the table's own natural business key post-migration (mirrors how `resources` and `delivery_centers` order by their own most-identifying column today, `name`) and produces a deterministic, human-meaningful order rather than insertion-order noise. Either choice resolves the Critical finding equally; this is a design preference, not a correctness requirement, and System Engineer may override to created_at at implementation time without needing another architecture round if a reason emerges.

backend_masterDataTables_js_entry.note_on_dropping_name: the current placeholder `name` field is replaced entirely by employeeId (the requirement gives resource_cost no independent 'name' concept once it's keyed to an employee) — System Engineer must confirm this against migration design: the existing `name not null` column either gets dropped in the same migration or, if any non-empty rows already exist and dropping is judged riskier than deprecating, the two-phase migration path in database.md (deprecate then remove) applies. Codebase-explorer's mapping did not report any existing resource_cost rows; if the table is empty, a direct drop in one migration is in-scope and preferred over an unnecessary two-phase deprecation for a table with no read-with-existing-data concern (database.md's two-phase rule exists to avoid breaking readers of live data, which does not apply to an empty placeholder table).

column_types.employee_id: integer not null — matches resources.employee_id's own type (integer, migration 0012) so the FK constraint and the equality join are type-compatible without casts.
column_types.offshore_cost: numeric, nullable, no default — optional per requirement, independently of onsite_cost.
column_types.onsite_cost: numeric, nullable, no default — same reasoning; requirement explicitly says do not enforce onsite-XOR-offshore at this layer.

migration_design_for_system_engineer.pattern_source: follows 0012_add_resource_columns.sql's shape (ADD COLUMN with a temporary default dropped immediately for the required column, since resource_cost may already hold placeholder rows whose name-only shape has no employee_id value to backfill with).
required_statements: alter table public.resource_cost add column employee_id integer not null default -1 (temporary sentinel default only to let ADD COLUMN succeed against any existing rows; must be dropped in the same migration file directly below, mirroring 0012's drop-default pattern) — or, if the table is confirmed empty, add column employee_id integer not null with no default needed at all; System Engineer confirms row count before finalizing which form to use.
alter table public.resource_cost alter column employee_id drop default (only needed if the sentinel-default form above was used).
alter table public.resource_cost add column offshore_cost numeric, add column onsite_cost numeric (nullable, no default, no drop-default step needed since they're optional).

alter table public.resource_cost drop column name (dropping the placeholder column now that employeeId supersedes it — see note_on_dropping_name above for the two-phase alternative if the table is not confirmed empty; this drop is now safe against the shared list query because masterDataRouter.js's ORDER BY is changed in the same code change to read `table.sortColumn ?? 'name'`, and resource_cost's descriptor sets sortColumn: 'employee_id' — see field_descriptor_extensions.sortColumn above. Whichever stage authors the migration and whichever stage edits masterDataRouter.js/masterDataTables.js MUST land together, or in an order where the router's fallback-to-'name' never executes against a resource_cost row that no longer has a name column).

alter table public.resource_cost add constraint resource_cost_employee_id_fkey foreign key (employee_id) references public.resources (employee_id) — the DB-level defense-in-depth constraint tech-lead required alongside the app-layer validateExists check; relies on resources.employee_id's existing unique constraint from migration 0012, which is what makes this FK meaningful.

create index ix_resource_cost_employee_id on public.resource_cost (employee_id) — required by database.md ('add an index on foreign keys') and doubles as the join-performance index for the lookups' LEFT JOIN.
migration_design_for_system_engineer.must_be_applied_live: per the task's instruction, this migration must be applied via mcp__Supabase__apply_migration by the stage that authors it (System Engineer/Engineer), not merely committed to disk — this SDD stage does not apply it, since no schema file has been written yet at this point in the pipeline.
migration_design_for_system_engineer.rls_and_trigger_conventions: resource_cost already has RLS-enabled-no-policies and the trg_resource_cost_updated_at trigger from migration 0011 — 0013 is a pure ADD/DROP COLUMN + constraint/index migration and must not touch either of those, consistent with 0012's treatment of resources.

resource_cost_entry_fields_change.label: the linked Resource's employee ID (Resources.employeeId) — must reference an existing Resource; the backend rejects a create/update with an employeeId that does not exist in Resources
offshore cost, in the company's standard currency unit — optional, independent of onsiteCost
onsite cost, in the company's standard currency unit — optional, independent of offshoreCost

mcp_layer_design.no_bespoke_mcp_code_needed: mcp-server/src/index.js already builds each add_/update_<slug> tool's zod shape generically off `fields[]` (z.number().finite() for type:'number', per the tool's own generation logic) — since employeeId/offshoreCost/onsiteCost are ordinary 'number' fields with no MCP-side existence concept, only the descriptor data above changes; add_resource_cost and update_resource_cost need no new code, matching tech-lead's 'MCP layer stays thin' direction.
mcp_layer_design.validation_enforced_once: the mcp-server calls the backend over HTTP (confirmed by tech-lead via apiClient.js) — the backend's 422 validation_error (from validateExists) or DB FK-violation-turned-422 propagates back through the existing HTTP-error-to-tool-error path unchanged; no duplicate validation logic is added on the MCP side, avoiding the two-mirrors-drifting-out-of-sync risk both enterprise-architect-pre and tech-lead flagged.
mcp_layer_design.name_field_removed: the current placeholder `{ key: 'name', ... }` field entry is removed from the resource_cost slug's fields[] in this mirror, matching the backend descriptor's replacement of name with employeeId/offshoreCost/onsiteCost.

frontend_design.column_order_rationale: employeeId first (the caller-supplied key, matches the Resources table's own column ordering convention where employeeId leads), then the two live-looked-up display fields immediately after (mirrors how a human would want to see 'who' before 'what it costs'), then the two cost fields, then ...AUDIT_COLUMNS unchanged (spread exactly as every other table does).
frontend_design.labeling_convention_match: 'Employee ID' / 'Employee Name' / 'Employee Designation' match FEAT-6's just-applied 'Employee <Field>' convention on the Resources table (commit 5b1f29b) exactly, including that employeeId itself does NOT get a redundant second 'Employee' prefix beyond what's already in the key name, consistent with how Resources' own employeeId column is labeled plain 'Employee ID' rather than 'Employee Employee ID'.
frontend_design.no_other_frontend_change_needed: the frontend is read-only (fetchMasterDataTable only GETs) and MasterDataTable renders whatever keys the GET response contains keyed by `columns[].key` — since employeeName/employeeDesignation arrive as ordinary top-level response keys via the backend's toResponse() lookup branch, no fetch logic, hook, or component behavior changes; this is a pure columns[] data change in one file.

api_contract.GET /v1/resource-cost and GET /v1/resour: response `data` now includes employeeId, employeeName, employeeDesignation (nullable if the referenced resource is missing/soft-deleted after the fact), offshoreCost, onsiteCost, plus the unchanged audit fields — 200, per api.md's existing single/collection envelope shapes, no change to those envelopes.
api_contract.POST /v1/resource-cost and PATCH /v1/res: request body takes employeeId (required on create, number), offshoreCost/onsiteCost (optional numbers, independently nullable). A body with employeeId not present in resources (or present but soft-deleted) is rejected 422 with `{ error: { code: 'validation_error', message: 'Request failed validation.', details: { employeeId: 'employeeId must reference an existing, non-deleted resources row.' } } }`, per api.md's error shape. employeeName/employeeDesignation in a request body are accepted but ignored (not part of `fields[]`), consistent with how any other unknown key is already ignored by the existing INSERT/UPDATE column-building logic.
api_contract.no_new_routes: no new endpoints are introduced — resource-cost keeps using the shared createMasterDataRouter(table) factory; only that factory's internals (validateExists check + lookups-aware SELECT) change to support the new descriptor kinds.

out_of_scope_for_this_feature: resource_deployment's own employeeId/lookup fields — tech-lead flagged this as a plausible future reuse of the same descriptors, not part of FEAT-5's requirement.
Any UI for writing resource-cost data — the task explicitly states writes happen only through the MCP server; the frontend dashboard stays read-only.
Enforcing onsite-XOR-offshore cost exclusivity — requirement explicitly says do not enforce this at this layer.
Auto-computing a derived 'total cost' or currency-formatting logic — not requested.
constraints_verified_against: database.md: FK existence validated at the service layer (validateExists in masterDataSchema.js/masterDataRouter.js, not the route handler in isolation) plus a real DB-level foreign key constraint as defense-in-depth; index added on the new foreign key (ix_resource_cost_employee_id); migrations never edit an existing file, 0013 is new.

api.md: 422 for validation failures (bad employeeId reference), consistent error envelope `{ error: { code, message, details } }`, no new routes, response/request schemas remain the shared master-data GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE shape.
frontend.md: masterDataApi.js columns[] change only — no component logic added, no inline styles, presentation-only file touched.

CLAUDE.md Core Principles: minimal-impact additive descriptor kinds (validateExists, lookups, sortColumn) rather than a bespoke resource-cost-only code fork; the other 8 master-data tables' SQL and validation paths are provably unchanged (all three gated behind `if (field.validateExists)` / `if (table.lookups)` / `table.sortColumn ?? 'name'`).

round_1_open_items_resolution.left_join_vs_inner_join: Resolved by architecture-critic: LEFT JOIN confirmed correct; the join predicate is fixed in this round to add `and j.deleted_at is null` so the stated soft-delete-null behavior actually holds (see field_descriptor_extensions.lookup.read_path_change above).
round_1_open_items_resolution.drop_name_outright_vs_two_phase_migratio: Resolved by architecture-critic: acceptable in principle for an empty placeholder table, contingent on System Engineer confirming row count at migration-authoring time. This round adds the binding requirement that the sortColumn fix lands in the same change set as the drop, per migration_design_for_system_engineer.required_statements above.
round_1_open_items_resolution.422_validation_error_shape_for_bad_emplo: Resolved by architecture-critic: the existing generic `validation_error` code with a per-field `details.employeeId` message is confirmed correct and consistent with the rest of the codebase; no bespoke `employee_not_found` code needed.

open_items_for_architecture_critic: Confirm the sortColumn table-descriptor fix (default 'name', resource_cost overriding to 'employee_id') fully resolves the Critical ORDER BY finding, and that its generality (opt-in per table, only resource_cost sets it, the other 8 tables' current query is provably unchanged) meets the same additive-only bar as validateExists/lookups.
Confirm the corrected LEFT JOIN predicate (`on j.employee_id = t.employee_id and j.deleted_at is null`) now matches the SDD's own stated soft-delete-null behavior with no remaining gap.
